questions.q: Why do Occupational Health and Safety practices need to be followed in a workplace?
options: To provide employees with a safe workplace
To ensure that employees are healthy in their workplace
To ensure that someone is trained as a first aid officer in all workplaces
To give employees an opportunity to complain to management about an unsafe workplace
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of OHS practices is to protect workers by providing a safe working environment. The other options describe narrow or incidental outcomes rather than the core reason for following OHS practices.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the ergonomic feature of a product?
options: It has a good shape and fit.
It is easy to work with and use.
It uses appropriate colour standards.
It requires minimum force to operate.
questions.explanation: Ergonomics is about fitting a product to the human user so it is comfortable, efficient and easy to work with and use. Shape, colour and force are individual factors but do not capture ergonomics as fully as overall ease of use.

questions.q: As a product approaches the end of its life cycle, what factor contributes most to its decline in acceptance?
options: Poor design
New materials
Shifting social trends
Changing manufacturing techniques
questions.explanation: As tastes, needs and fashions change, shifting social trends make a product less desirable and drive its decline at the end of its life cycle. Poor design, materials and manufacturing relate to how a product is made rather than why consumers stop accepting it over time.

questions.q: A delay in completing a design project is most likely to be caused by
options: poor timing.
poor planning.
lack of finance.
lack of resources.
questions.explanation: Effective project management relies on a realistic action and time plan; poor planning is the underlying cause that leads to missed deadlines and delays. Timing, finance and resources are factors that good planning is meant to manage.

questions.q: After developing a preliminary design concept, what would a designer do next?
options: Gather market research
Develop a technical illustration
Develop possible design solutions
Decide on manufacturing and production techniques
questions.explanation: Once a preliminary concept exists, the designer moves into ideation by developing and exploring possible design solutions. Market research comes earlier, while technical illustration and manufacturing decisions come later once a solution is chosen.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of developing sustainable technologies?
options: To reduce landfill
To have longer lasting products
To make better use of natural resources
To reduce the amount of materials used
questions.explanation: Sustainable technologies aim to use natural resources more efficiently so they remain available for future generations. Reducing landfill, extending product life and using fewer materials are specific benefits that flow from this overarching goal.

questions.q:
The following graphs show the results of market research about four target markets, A, B, C and D. Market size, disposable income and fear of technologies were investigated for each target market.

For which target market would a producer develop a next generation high-tech product?
options: A
B
C
D
questions.explanation: A next-generation high-tech product suits a market that can afford it and is comfortable with technology, so the producer chooses the market with high disposable income and a low fear of technologies. Interpreting the graphs identifies market D as the best fit.

questions.q: Which of the following best outlines an entrepreneur's activities in influencing the success of an innovation?
options: Examining durability and cultural factors
Analysing market research, legal and ethical issues
Analysing industry standards and production issues
Determining production costs and time management issues
questions.explanation: An entrepreneur takes a calculated risk to bring an innovation to market, so they focus on market research alongside the legal and ethical issues that affect its viability and acceptance. The other options describe production or technical concerns rather than the entrepreneur's market-focused role.

questions.q:
The evaluation of a product involves an examination of its features and/or functions.

Why is it necessary to conduct this evaluation?
options: To ensure that the greatest number of the product will sell
To determine whether the product is aesthetically pleasing
To ensure that the product performs all of its desired operations
To determine whether the product is a quality solution to the design problem
questions.explanation: Evaluation judges a product against the design criteria and brief to determine whether it is a quality solution to the design problem. Sales, aesthetics and function are individual measures, but the overall purpose of evaluation is to assess the product as a whole solution.

questions.q: Why does a designer need to consider the industrial and commercial practices that will be used during manufacturing?
options: To ensure the product will sell
To gain access to cheaper resources
To increase the product's rate of production
To produce products that meet market needs
questions.explanation: Understanding industrial and commercial manufacturing practices lets a designer plan for efficient mass production and a higher rate of production. The other options are commercial outcomes that depend on, but are not the direct reason for, considering these practices.
